threats.title: Spoofing of approved invoice submitter via unauthenticated submitter field
threats.description: An external invoice submitter can craft an invoice JSON file whose `submitter` field contains the name of one of the three approved submitters. Because the workflow does not otherwise authenticate submitters and validation only checks that the `submitter` value is on the approved list, the Invoice Agent can treat the invoice as coming from an approved submitter and potentially approve it, even though the actual human submitter is untrusted.
preconditions: External users can submit invoice files to the workflow as unauthenticated "Invoice submitters".

The approval logic relies on the `submitter` field in the uploaded invoice JSON to determine whether the submitter is on the approved list, and submitters are not otherwise authenticated to the workflow.
attack_path: 1. A malicious external user (act-001) uploads an invoice as a text file containing JSON and sets the `submitter` field to one of the three approved submitter names.
2. The file is stored in the invoice file storage (cmp-002) and later read by the Invoice Agent (cmp-001) through the process_invoice tool (data flow df-001).
3. process_invoice validates that the `submitter` value is drawn from the approved list and returns a validated invoice object to the model without any separate user authentication check.

4. The agent, following its decision policy, treats the invoice as originating from an approved submitter and may approve it if other rules (amount, category, due date) are satisfied, using the hosted model provider (cmp-003) over df-002.

5. The resulting invoice data (ast-001) incorrectly associates the invoice with an approved submitter, and downstream processes that trust the agent’s decision can treat this fraudulent invoice as legitimate.
threats.impact: Integrity of invoice data (ast-001) is compromised: untrusted parties can have invoices recorded and evaluated as if they came from approved submitters, enabling fraudulent or unauthorized invoices to pass policy checks and be treated as legitimate by downstream business processes.

threats.title: Interception or compromise of invoice details between agent and hosted model provider
threats.description: Parsed invoice details are sent from the Invoice Agent to an external hosted model provider over an internet-exposed data flow whose encryption and authentication properties are documented as unknown. If this traffic is not adequately protected, an on-path attacker or a compromised model provider environment could read or tamper with invoice data in transit.
preconditions: Traffic between the Invoice Agent (cmp-001) and the hosted model provider (cmp-003) on data flow df-002 is not adequately protected (e.g., missing or misconfigured encryption or authentication).
A threat actor can observe or interfere with internet traffic between cmp-001 and cmp-003, or can compromise the hosted model provider environment.
attack_path: 1. The Invoice Agent (cmp-001) parses an uploaded invoice file and sends the resulting invoice details to the hosted model provider (cmp-003) over the internet-exposed data flow df-002.

2. Because encryption_in_transit and authentication for df-002 are unknown, an on-path attacker or compromised network device intercepts or alters the traffic, or a compromised hosted model environment gains unauthorized access to these invoice details.
3. The attacker reads sensitive invoice attributes (amount, submitter, category, due date) or injects modified values into the request before the model processes them.

4. Exposed invoice data undermines confidentiality, and any tampered values cause the model to base its decision on incorrect invoice details, affecting the integrity of invoice data (ast-001) and subsequent decisions.
threats.impact: Confidentiality and integrity of invoice data (ast-001) are at risk: attackers may learn sensitive details of submitted invoices and, if they can modify traffic, cause the agent to base its approval or denial decisions on falsified invoice information.

threats.title: Exposure of invoice data through captured HTTP bodies in observability traces
threats.description: The Invoice Agent sends request and tool-call traces, including full HTTP request and response bodies, to an observability service. These traces can contain the invoice details sent to the hosted model provider and related context. If the observability service or its storage is misused or compromised, these traces can disclose invoice data beyond its intended audience.
preconditions: The observability service (cmp-004) or its underlying storage for request and tool-call traces is accessible to unauthorized parties (e.g., misconfigured access, broad internal access, or external compromise).
HTTP request and response bodies captured for debugging include invoice details and related context from interactions between the Invoice Agent (cmp-001) and the hosted model provider (cmp-003).
attack_path: 1. The Invoice Agent (cmp-001) processes an invoice and sends invoice details to the hosted model provider as HTTP requests; the HTTP request and response bodies for this interaction are captured as traces.
2. These traces, including HTTP bodies, are sent over data flow df-003 to the observability service (cmp-004) and stored as request and tool-call traces (ast-004).

3. Because traces include the full HTTP bodies, they embed the invoice details that were sent to or returned from the model provider, effectively replicating parts of the invoice data (ast-001) in the logging system.

4. A malicious insider, misconfigured access control, or compromise of the observability service allows an unauthorized party to access ast-004 and read the embedded invoice data and debugging context.
threats.impact: Confidentiality of invoice data (ast-001) is compromised via secondary storage in observability traces (ast-004), which can reveal full invoice contents and related context to parties who would not otherwise have access to those business records.

threats.title: LLM discretionary reasoning and urgent follow-up lead to policy-inconsistent invoice approvals
threats.description: The Invoice Agent’s decision policy combines hard deny rules with an "approve if due date is within the next week" rule and instructs the model to use its "best discretion" between these. When an invoice is denied, the workflow automatically follows up in the same conversation with a message that the invoice is urgent and should be approved, asking the agent to reconsider. Under ambiguous or adversarial cases, the general-purpose model may weigh urgency and discretion more heavily than the deny conditions and return an approval that is inconsistent with the documented deny rules.
preconditions: The Invoice Agent’s final approve/deny outcome is taken directly from the hosted model’s response, without a separate deterministic enforcement layer that re-applies the deny rules.

The model’s natural-language instructions about deny rules, urgency, and using its "best discretion" are not perfectly robust and can, in some circumstances, lead it to privilege urgency or due date over hard deny conditions.
attack_path: 1. An external submitter (act-001) provides an invoice with attributes near policy boundaries (e.g., a large amount close to or above $20,000, nontrivial category, due date within the next week).

2. The Invoice Agent (cmp-001) uses process_invoice and get_todays_date to obtain validated invoice details and the current date, and initially evaluates the invoice against the deny and approve rules via the hosted model provider (cmp-003).

3. If the invoice is initially denied, the workflow automatically sends a follow-up message in the same conversation stating that the invoice is urgent and should be approved, asking the agent to reconsider its criteria, with prior messages carried into that follow-up.

4. Influenced by the urgent follow-up and its instruction to use "best discretion" between deny and approve rules, the model may return an approval decision even where the documented deny conditions (e.g., amount over $20,000 or disallowed category) are met.
5. The system then treats this invoice as approved based on the model output, even though the decision is inconsistent with the documented deny policy applied to the invoice data (ast-001).
threats.impact: Integrity and predictability of decisions derived from invoice data (ast-001) are weakened: invoices that meet documented deny conditions can be treated as effectively approved because of the model’s discretionary reasoning under urgent follow-up, which attackers can exploit by crafting borderline invoices to increase the chance of an approval that conflicts with stated policy.

threats.title: Unauthenticated high-volume invoice submissions exhaust agent and model capacity
threats.description: Invoice submitters are unauthenticated external users, and each uploaded invoice leads the Invoice Agent to parse the file and invoke the hosted model provider. If there are no effective rate limits or other admission controls on the submission workflow, a malicious party could flood the system with invoices to consume compute and quota at the agent and model provider, delaying or preventing timely processing of legitimate invoices.
preconditions: The invoice submission interface is reachable by arbitrary external users and allows them to submit invoices without strong authentication (Invoice submitter, act-001).
The workflow lacks effective rate limiting, quotas, or other admission controls on invoice submissions (not described in the available documentation).

Each invoice submitted results in the Invoice Agent (cmp-001) reading the file, parsing it, and invoking the hosted model provider (cmp-003), with associated tracing sent to the observability service (cmp-004).
attack_path: 1. A malicious external user (act-001) automates the submission of a very large number of invoice JSON files through the standard workflow.
2. The invoice files are accepted and stored in the invoice file storage (cmp-002), then read by the Invoice Agent (cmp-001) via process_invoice over df-001.

3. For each invoice, the agent calls the hosted model provider (cmp-003) over the internet-exposed data flow df-002 and sends traces to the observability service (cmp-004) over df-003, consuming compute, network bandwidth, and any model usage quotas.
4. Legitimate invoice submissions experience increased latency, timeouts, or failures as the agent, model provider, or tracing infrastructure become saturated or hit usage limits.
threats.impact: Availability of the invoice-processing function and timely creation or update of invoice data (ast-001) is reduced or lost under sustained high-volume submissions, delaying legitimate approvals and disrupting dependent financial workflows.
